pages.name: Brackets as a rectangle
pages.text: This rectangle is `x + 3` wide and `x + 2` tall, so its area is `(x + 3)(x + 2)`. Cutting each side where its `x` part ends makes four tiles, which add up to `x² + 5x + 6`. At `x = 4` both make 42, and sliding `x` keeps them equal.

Lines from the splits cut it into 4 tiles: x squared of 16, 3x of 12, 2x of 8, 6 of 6. x plus 3 x plus 2 equals x squared plus 3x plus 2x plus 6. equals x squared plus 5x plus 6. x plus 3 x plus 2 makes 7 times 6 equals 42. x squared plus 3x plus 2x plus 6 makes 16 plus 12 plus 8 plus 6 equals 42.

pages.name: Four tiles
pages.task: Writing the brackets as their tiles added up is [[expanding]] them. Expand `(x + 4)(x + 1)`.
pages.why: The tiles are `x²`, `4x`, `x` and 4, as `4 × 1` is 4. The strips collect to `4x + x = 5x`, so the answer is `x² + 5x + 4`. At `x = 2` both make 18.

pages.name: Drag the sides
pages.text: Drag the knob at the end of each side to change its number. The strips are always each number times `x`, and the corner is the two numbers multiplied. A two-term bracket like `x + 5` is a [[binomial]], and a rule with `x²` as its highest power is a [[quadratic]].

pages.name: Square it
pages.task: Someone wrote `(x + 3)² = x² + 9`, but at `x = 2` that makes 13, not 25. Which answer puts back the tiles they left out?
pages.why: They left out both strips of `3x`, `6x` in all. The square is `x²`, two strips of `3x` and a corner of `3 × 3 = 9`, so the answer is `x² + 6x + 9`, and at `x = 2` both make 25.

pages.name: A minus sign
pages.text: No side can be `−4` long, so with a minus sign the rectangle becomes a grid. Each cell is its column times its row, sign and all, just as `x(x + 1) − 4(x + 1)` expands, and a cell below zero is hatched. The cells collect to `x² − 3x − 4`.

pages.name: A minus on the side
pages.task: Now the minus is in the second bracket. Expand `(x + 5)(x − 2)`.
pages.why: The cells are `x²`, `−2x`, `5x` and `5 × −2 = −10`. The two `x` cells collect to `5x − 2x = 3x`, so the answer is `x² + 3x − 10`. At `x = 3` both make 8.

pages.name: Mixed: a squared minus
pages.task: One more mix. Expand `(x − 6)²`, which means `(x − 6)(x − 6)`.
pages.why: The cells are `x²`, `−6x`, `−6x` and `−6 × −6 = 36`. The two `x` cells collect to `−12x`, so the answer is `x² − 12x + 36`. At `x = 2` both make 16.
